aiOverview.content: The 2026 United Airlines NYC Half Marathon follows a 13.1-mile point-to-point course that starts on Washington Avenue near the Brooklyn Museum and finishes in Central Park. This "park-to-park" route takes over 30,000 runners through Brooklyn and Manhattan, featuring major landmarks such as the Brooklyn Bridge, FDR Drive, and Times Square. Course Breakdown The race is divided into three primary segments as runners move from Brooklyn into Manhattan: Brooklyn Start and Prospect Park: Runners begin on Washington Avenue (near Sullivan Place) and head into Prospect Park. The route includes a loop through the park, involving the challenge of Battle Pass Hill, before exiting toward Grand Army Plaza. The Bridge and FDR Drive: After exiting the park, runners head down Flatbush Avenue to cross the Brooklyn Bridge using the Manhattan-bound roadway. Once in Manhattan, the course follows the FDR Drive North for approximately 4 miles, providing views of the East River and the United Nations. Midtown and Central Park Finish: Participants exit the FDR at 42nd Street and head west, passing Grand Central Terminal. The route turns north onto 7th Avenue to run through a traffic-free Times Square. The race enters Central Park at 59th Street and finishes on West Drive near 72nd Street. Key Locations and Timing Expand map Zoom in Zoom out Official Course Cutoff Times To ensure the reopening of city streets, runners must maintain a minimum pace of approximately 13:45 per mile to meet specific checkpoint deadlines: LocationMile MarkCutoff TimeBrooklyn Bridge (via Brooklyn Bridge Blvd.)4.110:20 a.m.FDR-bound off-ramp (to access FDR Drive)5.410:40 a.m.FDR Drive Exit (to access 42nd St.)9.411:45 a.m.Finish Line (Central Park)13.11:30 p.m. Notable Features Terrain: The course is primarily paved and urban, with rolling segments in Central Park and moderate inclines on the bridges. Unique Access: This is the only race in history that utilizes the Manhattan-bound roadway of the Brooklyn Bridge. Event Scale: The 2026 race set a record as the largest half marathon in NYRR history with over 30,000 finishers.
